doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Quoting the lyric and Eddie Arkin's chord changes
summary: Rowe quizzes her on lyric lines and reads chord changes from the song.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well it’s pure poetry. I’m going to read a — I’m going to test your memory, I’m going to read a phrase and I’m going to ask you to answer with the appropriate phrase.
Okay. “To pick the lock that guards the place”
“Of dark and light of time and space” or something like that?
Correct. “That I could” — no I’m sorry – “Where an answer might be found.”
“That I could wrap my head around.”
No one’s ever quizzed me in an interview before.

You get to move on to the next round. But you know I had this really odd image because about the time I was looking into this song, and I downloaded the piano music about the same time I passed by one of these big white boards that are in Hamilton just on the walls where students study. And it had that typical, either it was chemistry or it was physics or something, you know the black — I mean the whole board like this unending calculation. And then I looked at Eddie Arkin’s chord changes and I’m going to read just four of them.
A flat minor 6–9 major seven, G 13 sharp 9, G flat 13 flat 9, F minor 6-9 add 11 in a measure of 3/2. These are chord changes but they also might be the secret of life, I don’t know.
